title: Director of Marketplace at Walmart eCommerce Sees Muse as a Potential Source of Incremental Demand but Expects Retailers to Protect Checkout and Customer Relationships
expert: Director, Marketplace at Walmart eCommerce (current; retailer view of agent integrations, Meta fee intentions second-hand); interview 2026-10-22
verdict: A Walmart marketplace director sees Muse as incremental discovery but expects retailers to protect checkout; Meta direct checkout carries no additional channel fee today, and planned transaction fees risk deterring thin-margin merchants.

Muse/agent monetization: no additional channel fee today on Meta direct checkout (hearsay), so Muse transaction revenue is still ahead; Muse >10M US/Canada users, >25% shopping weekly (SB #62031). → Tenet 3 (Muse $5B+) ↓
retailers have spent years optimizing checkout and will not cede it, consistent with ~1/3 of tested US sites blocking Muse (SB #60946). → Tenet 3 (Muse $5B+) ↓
Amazon absence could shift Muse shoppers to Walmart, consistent with Amazon reportedly blocking Muse (SB #60946). → Tenet 3 (Muse $5B+) →

changes: Retailers protecting checkout vs Jefferies: ~1/3 of tested US websites block Muse, Amazon included (SB #60946): consistent.
No additional channel fee on direct checkout today vs Muse >10M US/Canada users and >25% of weekly users shopping (SB #62031): usage without monetization yet.
thesis_impact: Tenet 3 (Muse $5B+): ↓ — no channel fee yet, planned fees could deter thin-margin merchants, and retailers resist instant checkout.
